text:
Maya: Hey folks — finishing up onboarding. I need Vault access for product-search and KMS key use for a local demo. Who should I ask and what's the quickest path?

devex-bot: Hi Maya! Welcome 🎉. Start with the onboarding checklist: https://redwood.internal/onboarding/vault. Quick summary: for Vault access open a 'vault-access' issue in the infra repo with team name, secret paths, and why. For KMS requests, file in #eng-security with intended usage. Manager approval is required for production paths.

Maya: Thanks! Can I get a temporary token for local dev instead of full prod access? Want to demo without waiting for the full workflow.

Alex: @Maya yes — we commonly issue 24h temp tokens for new hires. You can run this locally if you have the right cli perms:

  vault token create -policy=newhire -ttl=24h -display-name="maya.local"

Or ping me and I'll create one.

Maya: If you can create it that'd be great, @Alex. Also, which paths will I be able to read for product-search?

Jordan: For dev/demo we usually give read to /secret/data/product-search and /transit/unwrap for KMS testing. Note: production service accounts and keys require a separate security request and rotation plan. Our default rotation cadence is 90 days (30 days for high-sensitivity service keys).

Maya: Got it — who signs the security request for production?

Tia: @Maya I can approve your access for product-search dev paths. For production keys we need the service owner + security to OK. Tia here (your manager) — I approve the dev-level access.

Alex: Done — created a 24h token for you and DM'd the value. I also added you to the 'product-search' Vault group so you can see secrets under /secret/data/product-search. Verify with:

  vault kv get secret/data/product-search/demo-creds

Maya: I received the DM and can read the demo creds. Thanks so much. One more question: what's the recommended flow to rotate a secret that's KMS-wrapped?

Jordan: Short flow: 1) create a new key version (or new key) in KMS; 2) decrypt and re-encrypt secrets with the new key (we use a rewrap job for this); 3) update service configs to reference the new key; 4) revoke the old key version once services are using the new one. If you want I can run through it with you on Monday.

Tia: Also add a brief note to your onboarding doc listing which secrets you accessed and any demo creds you used. Helps with audits.

Maya: Will do. Really appreciate the quick help — this made setup painless :heart:
